title: Feature flag + gradual enablement plan for Hosted canary rollouts (Console UI)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
We need a GA-safe enablement plan for the Hosted canary rollouts workflow (Console wizard + rollout details pages) that supports:
- Internal dogfood first (Redwood tenants)
- Per-tenant beta enablement (design partner allowlist)
- Staged GA rollout (progressive enablement across all tenants)
- Clear kill switch behavior that is safe even during an active rollout

This ticket is focused on feature flagging + release mechanics (Console + Console backend + control plane integration points), not the core routing enforcement or orchestrator state machine.

Context:
- The canary workflow touches Console UI, Console backend orchestration endpoints, policy engine guardrails, routing enforcement, and telemetry.
- We need the ability to disable the UI independently from disabling rollout actions, and we need a backstop kill switch that prevents any new canary traffic splits from being applied if we detect risk.

Goals
1) Separate flags for:
   a) UI visibility (wizard entry points, “Create rollout” CTA)
   b) API/action gating (create/start/progress/rollback endpoints)
   c) Data plane enforcement (traffic split application)
2) Per-tenant enablement with an allowlist for beta and an easy path to GA ramp.
3) Explicit “kill switch” semantics and runbook steps that do not require code deploy to activate.
4) Clear monitoring checklist during staged rollout + crisp backout steps.

Non-goals
- Implementing the policy engine itself (tracked in ENG-9146)
- Implementing routing primitive / cohorting (tracked in ENG-9123)
- Creating dashboards (tracked in ENG-9152 / PRs in observability pack)

Proposed flag design
A) Console UI flag (controls visibility only)
- Flag name: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui
- Scope: tenant
- Default: OFF
- Behavior:
  - OFF: Hide “Rollouts” entry point for Hosted routes; do not show wizard; hide rollout create CTA.
  - ON: Show UI; still requires API/action flag ON to actually perform mutations.

B) Console backend action flag (controls mutation endpoints)
- Flag name: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_actions
- Scope: tenant
- Default: OFF
- Behavior:
  - OFF: Return 403 with a structured error (feature_not_enabled) for:
    - create rollout
    - start rollout
    - progress step
    - pause/resume
    - rollback
  - OFF should still allow READ-only endpoints if the tenant already has historical rollout objects (important for support / audit views).

C) Control plane / routing enforcement flag (backstop kill switch)
- Flag name: platform.hosted_canary_rollouts_enforcement
- Scope: global + per-tenant override (global OFF is hard stop)
- Default: OFF in staging, OFF in prod until beta start date
- Behavior:
  - If global OFF: do not apply canary split configs in data plane; all traffic goes to baseline. Orchestrator should still be able to transition state to “Paused (enforcement disabled)” with a clear reason.
  - If global ON but tenant override OFF: same as above for that tenant.
  - Notes:
    - This flag must be evaluated at the data plane enforcement point (ENG-9123) and should be fail-closed in the direction of safety (i.e., if flag service is unreachable, treat as OFF and route all traffic to baseline).
    - We must document expected impact on existing in-flight rollouts (see “Kill switch semantics”).

Kill switch semantics (must be documented + tested)
- UI kill switch (A) is purely cosmetic: turning it OFF hides UI entry points but does not stop a running rollout.
- Actions kill switch (B) prevents new changes from Console, but does not stop enforcement.
- Enforcement kill switch (C) is the emergency stop. Turning it OFF should:
  1) Immediately stop canary traffic from being served (baseline gets 100%).
  2) Preserve the rollout object + timeline; do NOT delete.
  3) Orchestrator behavior:
     - If an auto-stop is triggered while enforcement is OFF, orchestrator should still be able to pause/rollback states, but those states are mostly bookkeeping. We should present a clear banner in Console: “Traffic splitting is currently disabled by an operator. Canary traffic is not being served.”
  4) Audit logging:
     - Flag flips are not currently in customer audit logs. We should at minimum log an internal audit event (SRE/operator audit log) when (C) changes. (If that’s out of scope for GA, document it clearly as an internal-only action.)

Enablement phases (beta → GA)
Phase 0: Pre-beta (staging + internal dev)
- console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui: ON for Redwood internal tenant(s) in staging
- console.hosted_canary_rollouts_actions: ON for Redwood internal tenant(s) in staging
- platform.hosted_canary_rollouts_enforcement: ON in staging only
- Goal: validate end-to-end workflow without exposing to external tenants

Phase 1: Internal dogfood (prod)
- Enable A + B for Redwood internal tenant(s) in prod
- Keep enforcement (C) ON globally but set conservative alerting + on-call awareness; confirm kill switch works in prod.
- Guardrails:
  - Require manual approvals for >5% step for internal dogfood
  - Default auto-stop thresholds on (ENG-9158), but tune to avoid alert storms

Phase 2: Design partner beta (prod allowlist)
- Enable A + B for allowlisted tenants only (per beta tracker)
- Keep enforcement (C) ON globally; keep the ability to flip OFF globally if we see systemic issue
- Operational requirements:
  - Support channel routing defined (on-call + #eng-sre + #support escalations)
  - Daily check on cohort dashboards for enabled tenants

Phase 3: Limited GA (progressive ramp)
- Keep (C) ON globally
- Ramp A + B using staged allowlist expansions:
  - 5% of eligible tenants → 25% → 50% → 100%
- Eligibility definition (initial):
  - Hosted routes only
  - Tenants with RBAC bundle version including rollout-approver (if approvals enabled)
  - Tenants not opted-out of beta features (if we have a general “beta” toggle)

Phase 4: Full GA
- Set A + B defaults to ON for all tenants
- Keep (C) default ON globally, but maintain kill switch operational ownership with SRE/Release on-call.

Implementation details
- Flag evaluation location:
  - A: Console frontend (feature gate routing/UI)
  - B: Console backend (authoritative gate on mutations)
  - C: Data plane / routing config evaluation (authoritative kill switch)
- Flag service: use existing FeatureFlagService (ffsvc) + per-tenant overrides.
- Error handling:
  - When B is OFF, return consistent error code that Console can render:
    - code=FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED, feature=hosted_canary_rollouts, docs_link=…
- Telemetry:
  - Emit counter for blocked actions due to feature flag (to detect confusion / misconfig)
  - Add logs for enforcement flag OFF events at routing layer to support incident debugging

Risks / edge cases
- Partial availability: UI ON but actions OFF creates confusion. Mitigation: Console should detect (B) OFF and show a callout “Your org is not enabled yet. Contact support.”
- A tenant with existing rollouts when flags turn OFF: must preserve read paths; don’t hard-404.
- Flag propagation delays: if (C) flip OFF isn’t immediate, kill switch isn’t useful. Need SLO/expectation for propagation (or implement a cached short TTL + push invalidation).
- Multi-region behavior: ensure (C) is applied consistently in all regions; if one region still serves canary, we can get inconsistent cohort metrics and customer-visible behavior.

Deliverables
- Documented enablement plan (this ticket) + runbook snippet for Release/SRE
- Flag definitions added to ffsvc registry + Console/backend integration
- Console UX behavior for not-enabled states and enforcement-disabled banner
- Basic test coverage (unit/integration) for A/B/C gating paths
- Checklist for GA day (who flips what, when, and what to monitor)

References
- Design partner enablement/how-to: sources/confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/how-to-enable-hosted-canary-rollouts-for-a-tenant.json
- Release checklist draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json
- Related: ENG-9123 (data plane enforcement), ENG-9140 (orchestrator), ENG-9158 (auto-stop/rollback)
acceptance_criteria: Feature flags A/B/C are defined with clear ownership, defaults, scope, and documented semantics
Console frontend is gated by console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui (no dead links / hidden entry points when OFF)
Console backend blocks all rollout mutation actions when console.hosted_canary_rollouts_actions is OFF (read-only still works)
Data plane enforcement respects platform.hosted_canary_rollouts_enforcement as a global kill switch and fails safe to baseline
Console shows clear messaging when UI is ON but actions are OFF (not enabled) and when enforcement is disabled (traffic not being split)
Enablement phases (internal → beta allowlist → GA ramp) are written with explicit steps and owners
Backout steps are documented and do not require a deploy (flag flip only), including what happens to running rollouts
A minimal monitoring checklist is included (which dashboards, what thresholds, who to page)
comments: 2025-02-20 — Dylan Brooks: Drafting flag split into UI vs actions vs enforcement. We’ve been bitten before by “UI-only” flags; want backend to be authoritative on mutations. Will propose 3 flags and have data plane treat kill switch as fail-closed-to-baseline.

2025-02-24 — Mina Haddad: +1 on enforcement gate at routing layer. If kill switch is only in Console, it’s useless during an incident. Please ensure the enforcement flag is evaluated per-request or from config refresh with low TTL; don’t rely on long-lived cached config.

2025-02-25 — Sean Gallagher: For prod: we need a single global OFF switch we can flip during an incident without hunting for tenant overrides. Also please document what operators should expect to see in metrics when enforcement is OFF (baseline goes to 100%, canary cohort metrics drop).

2025-03-03 — Chloe Martin: Backend gating: I’ll add FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED structured errors for all mutation endpoints. Read endpoints should stay accessible; we have support cases where customers need to screenshot timelines after we disable features.

2025-03-07 — Tessa Morgan: UX request: if UI is enabled but actions are blocked, show a banner explaining “Beta access required” and a link to docs/support. Also, for enforcement-disabled, use a strong warning state on the rollout details page so customers don’t think the rollout is progressing.

2025-03-12 — Connor O'Brien: For staged GA ramp, we’ll start with allowlist expansion (manual) before we flip defaults. Please include a GA-day checklist: which flags flip in what order, and who is on point (Release + SRE).

2025-03-18 — Dylan Brooks: Added staged rollout phases + explicit kill switch semantics. Remaining question: do we need internal audit logs for enforcement flag flips? If we can’t ship customer-visible audit for it, we should at least log to operator audit trail. Marcus/Kevin—please advise.

2025-03-21 — Marcus Lin: Customer-visible audit logging of feature flag flips is out of scope; internal operator audit is recommended. At minimum, log an internal security event with actor + timestamp when the global enforcement kill switch changes. Don’t block GA on it, but capture in follow-up if not landed.

2025-03-24 — Dylan Brooks: Marking In Review. Plan is stable; waiting for final sign-off from SRE (Sean/Rafael) on propagation expectations and from Release (Connor) on ramp steps. Next: align with ENG-9123 implementation on fail-closed behavior.
